core_obligations: Show that consecutive composites vanish, case by case: a positive scalar curvature bordism of a boundary is a boundary in the relative group; a closed spin manifold with positive scalar curvature metric is null-bordant in the relative group via the cylinder; and the boundary map sends the absolute bordism group into classes represented by empty boundaries (proof lines 377-400).

Show the reverse inclusions of kernels in images, again case by case: a class in the absolute group mapping to zero in the relative group admits a null-bordism whose other part carries a positive scalar curvature metric, giving a preimage in the positive group; a class in the positive group mapping to zero in the absolute group is filled by a bordism that represents a preimage in the relative group (proof lines 402-425).

Close the last exactness: a relative class mapping to zero in the positive group admits a second bordism agreeing on the boundary, and gluing the two along that boundary gives a closed manifold whose cylinder is a bordism showing that the class lies in the image of the absolute group (proof lines 426-431).
proof_roadmap: Prove that each composite of two consecutive maps vanishes, using the explicit description of the three maps (proof lines 377-400).
Construct preimages for each of the three inclusions kernel-in-image, the last one by gluing two bordisms along their common boundary (proof lines 402-431).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that the three equivariant bordism groups defined earlier fit into a G-equivariant version of the Stolz positive scalar curvature exact sequence, with the three maps given by taking the boundary, forgetting the metric, and viewing a closed manifold as a manifold with empty boundary (statement lines 367-376). The proof is a complete case-by-case verification: it first checks that each composite of two consecutive maps vanishes, then constructs an explicit preimage for every class that lies in a kernel, the last case by gluing two bordisms along their common boundary and passing to the cylinder of the resulting closed manifold (proof lines 377-431). The step that carries the content is the last inclusion, since it requires building a bordism in the relative group out of two given ones; the other five verifications are direct consequences of the definitions. The argument is self-contained, the citation being only a pointer to the non-equivariant statement. H2.
